steps.what: Review designs and assemble versioned requirements, calculation inputs and estimate assumptions
Recalculate totals and compare specified values against recorded limits
Judge engineering adequacy, investigate discrepancies and approve the exact reviewed submission

tasks.design: Configure a checked {SPREADSHEET} to rerun arithmetic and explicit limit comparisons from the engineer's review register. The engineer still reviews model validity, risks and exclusions in {DOCS} before approving a specific submission.
tasks.previous_blocker: Inputs and limits were dispersed across design revisions and quote documents.
tasks.enabler_now: Native formula checks and revision identifiers support repeatable numerical comparisons.
tasks.still_hard: A numerically consistent design can be physically unsuitable or incomplete.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer judges adequacy and resolves conflicting requirements.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic repetition; technical approval rights stay the same.

reach.learn: Trace a review finding to its exact drawing revision.

evidence.claim: Relatics supports requirements and verification records; this does not establish robotic design correctness.
Native arithmetic checking and the labour estimates are model knowledge, unmeasured for this role.

assumptions: Boundary is the engineer's review, excluding creation of the original design and supplier pricing.

In s1 the engineer produces revision IDs, requirement IDs, quantities, units, unit prices, formula inputs, limits and source references; all capture and applicability checks are counted. Missing fields return to manual review before s2.
Test native spreadsheet controls before custom code; solver runtime earns no labour saving.
unknowns: Share of reviews with repeatable numerical checks
research_questions: Can independent review examples expose wrong units and outdated limits?

already_counted.description: Input capture and engineering approval remain fully counted.

incremental.description: Maintain and independently check calculation templates.

approvals.approved_version: Submission revision, input register and check report hashes; any change voids approval.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80 gross=20 net=13 after 7 upkeep. Zero if numerical checks already run automatically; 3 if only a small repeated estimate portion benefits.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Process and interpret robotic sensor signals

steps.what: Inspect signals and establish channel mappings, calibration context and valid processing settings
Apply specified filters and derive signal summaries using the signal analysis workbench
Interpret sensor results against raw traces and investigate artifacts or unexpected physical behaviour

tasks.design: Use saved processing recipes in the signal analysis workbench {OTHER} for transformations the engineer has specified. Preserve raw traces and processing settings so the engineer can distinguish physical findings from filtering artifacts.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated setup and transformations were performed interactively.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved recipes can replay explicit processing settings without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Calibration errors, aliasing and changing operating conditions can defeat apparently sensible summaries.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer interprets physical meaning and uncertainty.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated transformation setup; interpretation responsibility is unchanged.

reach.learn: Agree channel naming and calibration provenance without transferring uncounted capture work.

evidence.claim: Saved signal-processing recipes are model knowledge; no digest case establishes labour savings for robotics signal interpretation.

assumptions: Boundary starts with recordings already acquired; acquisition and live robot control are outside this task and receive no savings.

In s1 the engineer produces file IDs, channel mappings, units, sample rates, time alignment, calibration versions, filter settings, rejected intervals and reference traces, with capture and checking counted. Missing provenance triggers manual investigation rather than automatic processing.
OTHER means the signal analysis workbench. Test native batch recipes first; existing unattended computation is not baseline labour.
research_questions: Do replayed transformations preserve known transient events and identify missing channels?

already_counted.description: Recipe inputs and physical interpretation are retained.

incremental.description: Revalidate recipes when sensors or sampling change.
Test support maintains recording export compatibility.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=75 gross=25 net=17 after 8 upkeep. Zero when processing is already scripted; 4 when only repeated interactive setup is removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Reproduce robotics faults and inspect code, traces and equipment behaviour in a safe test environment
Diagnose causes, revise programs and validate the correction against observed behaviour

tasks.design: Keep fault reproduction and correction with the engineer using the robot development environment {OTHER}. Use its existing debugger and test tools; introducing generated corrections lacks a demonstrated advantage for these hardware-dependent faults.
tasks.previous_blocker: The difficulty is reproducing behaviour and distinguishing code faults from mechanical or sensing faults.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing debugging tools assist inspection but do not remove the diagnostic judgement.
tasks.still_hard: A correction may fix one scenario while introducing unsafe behaviour elsewhere.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer selects discriminating tests and judges the correction.
tasks.altitude: No assumed change in weekly effort or deployment authority.

reach.learn: Coordinate safe reproduction and separate hardware and software hypotheses.

evidence.claim: Siemens Industrial Copilot can draft PLC code and HMI screens; this does not demonstrate safe debugging of arbitrary robotics programs.

assumptions: Boundary covers fault reproduction through a checked development revision; production deployment is separately authorised and excluded.
OTHER is the robot development environment. Engineer captures observations and test outcomes within the retained steps; no free structured fault classification is assumed.
Consider native debugger improvements first. Zero incremental upkeep because this proposal adds no tool, model or workflow.
unknowns: Controller types and reproducibility of faults
research_questions: Which recurring fault classes could benefit from native trace capture without adding capture effort?

already_counted.description: Diagnosis, correction and validation remain fully counted.

approvals.approved_version: Exact source revision, robot configuration and validation results; changes require revalidation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Hardware-dependent debugging remains unchanged; no assumed generic coding speedup.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Build, configure and test robots under controlled conditions against engineering requirements

tasks.design: Retain physical assembly, configuration and validation with the engineer using the robot test bench {OTHER}. Native controls support the work, but the task offers no established removable administrative component.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical integration and unexpected interactions demand supervised engineering work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing bench tools support tests without removing physical verification.
tasks.still_hard: Real equipment can diverge from simulations and test plans.
tasks.human_edge: The engineer recognises unsafe or unexplained behaviour and stops testing.
tasks.altitude: Hands-on engineering and acceptance responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Coordinate test boundaries and stop conditions.

evidence.claim: Retaining physical robotic integration and validation is model knowledge; no measured saving is asserted.

assumptions: Boundary covers hands-on build, configuration and testing; design reviews and program debugging elsewhere must not be counted again.
OTHER means robot test bench. The engineer produces observations and disposition during s1; no automatic readiness or safety flag is assumed.
Existing native bench configuration is considered first. Zero added upkeep because no new automation or capture contract is introduced.
research_questions: Is there a separately observable repeated test setup burden before proposing an automation baseline?

already_counted.description: All physical work, observation and disposition are retained.

approvals.approved_version: Exact robot configuration, test conditions and disposition record; modifications require new evaluation.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=100 gross=0 net=0. Physical build and validation remain fully counted without an invented paperwork baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Numerical preparation can shrink while physical engineering and acceptance remain central.
reach: Coordinate traceable test inputs with robotics technicians and design engineers.
role.ambitious_version: An engineer who spends less effort replaying calculations and more effort testing assumptions.
